answer: Use a slashable, per-identity survey bond as the sybil defense. Each account claims a distinct reef plot and commits a survey image showing its fixed basalt marker beside an umber calibration tile; auditors receive randomly chosen plots and compare fresh images with the committed geometry and color. Reused images, overlapping plots, or missing markers burn that account’s bond. A cheater multiplying accounts must finance separate bonds and maintain separate auditable plots rather than cloning a submission.
